dashboard.label: ITSI Setup
dashboard.description: How to install IT Service Intelligence (Splunkbase app 1841) by extracting its .spl — the only supported method.

html.p: ITSI is a premium, separately-licensed Splunk app (Splunkbase app 1841) — it isn't committed to the repo (licensing + size), so it's installed from your own .spl. Per Splunk's docs it installs only by extracting the package into etc/apps — this page shows the repeatable ways to do that automatically.

Heads-up: ITSI is heavy (its own indexes, KV store, saved searches, ML deps) and needs a run-time license (trial or purchased). On this reset-each-session VM you'll re-do this after every reset. For a lighter demo of the same idea, use the interim "Service Health" dashboard instead.

search.query: | rest /services/apps/local | search title=itsi OR title=SA-ITOA OR label="*Service Intelligence*" | eval Status="installed" | table title label version Status

html.p: Per Splunk's own docs, ITSI (Splunkbase app 1841) does not support installation via Splunk Web or the splunk install app command. The only supported method is to extract the .spl into $SPLUNK_HOME/etc/apps (stop Splunk → untar → start). The .spl is just a gzip tarball, so this is exactly what our boot install does — ITSI installs the same way as any other app here, with no file-moving.
(The Splunk-10 Web UI also has a hard 512 MB upload cap that max_upload_size can't lift — but even below that size, the UI path is unsupported for ITSI regardless.)
html.h3: Install it (pick one — both extract into etc/apps at boot)
html.p: A) Auto-fetch from a URL (any account) — recommended: host your ITSI .spl where the lab can reach it, then run apply.sh — it prompts for Direct URL(s) of .spl/.tgz apps (or set SPLUNK_INSTALL_URLS), fetches it, and extracts it into etc/apps before Splunk starts. Re-installs on every reset; nothing is committed to the repo.
B) Splunkbase auto-download (if entitled): add ITSI's app id to the boot install; the downloader extracts it into etc/apps the same way.
First Splunkbase download needs the app's terms accepted once in a browser (app 1841), or the API returns HTTP 403.
C) Manual, if the .spl is already on the box (the documented steps):
html.pre: sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk stop sudo -u splunk tar -xf /tmp/splunk-it-service-intelligence_501.spl -C /opt/splunk/etc/apps sudo -u splunk /opt/splunk/bin/splunk start
html.p: Do not use splunk install app for ITSI — it is explicitly unsupported and can leave a broken install.

ul.li: Java 8-11 or 17 — required for anomaly detection + notable-event management. apply.sh auto-installs openjdk-17 when it sees the itsi app (Ubuntu 24.04's default JRE is 21, which ITSI does not support, so 17 is pinned).
Default admin user must exist (it does here) — deleting or renaming it breaks ITSI.
ITSI can't share a search head with Enterprise Security or IT Essentials Work — neither is installed here.

ol.li: License: ITSI needs its own license. Add a trial/eval under Settings ▸ Licensing if prompted, or ITSI runs in a limited/trial state.
First run: open the IT Service Intelligence app — it completes a one-time setup and creates its indexes (e.g. itsi_summary) + KV store.
Point it at lab data: create a couple of Services (e.g. "London Hosts", "Berlin Hosts") with KPIs from our metrics/syslog (index=*_metrics, index=*_linux) to get glass tables and health scores.

html.p: RBAC note: ITSI has its own role model; the lab's location roles won't automatically map to ITSI service access.

html.h3: Making it survive the session reset
html.p: The VM wipes each session, so a manual install is lost. Both boot options below re-install automatically on every reset — no file-moving:

ul.li: URL auto-fetch (any account) — set SPLUNK_INSTALL_URLS="https://your-host/itsi.spl" (or answer the prompt) when running apply.sh. Works regardless of Splunkbase entitlement; it still needs an ITSI run-time license after install.

Splunkbase auto-download — if your splunk.com account is entitled to ITSI, add its Splunkbase app id (1841) to the boot install: SPLUNKBASE_APP_IDS="1841" when running apply.sh (same flow as the MCP Server). First download of any Splunkbase app needs its license terms accepted once in a browser at splunkbase.splunk.com while logged in, or the API returns HTTP 403.

html.p: Version check: make sure your ITSI build supports Splunk 10.4 — if the app won't load after restart, that's the usual cause.
